Messages.Author: quetzalcoatl
Messages.Body:
Mata Hari is not that complicated. The exact situations that she comes
up in can be mirrored by previous "tricks" in play.

I think that she was invented as a vampire that could perform these
"tricks".

Tricks I speak of are:

Clan Impersonate to play other clan cards.

Out of the Frying Pan/Into the Fire to play Cam/Sab cards.

Vampire A recruits clan-only retainer/equipment that doesn't limit it
to that clan after equipping (Sword of Nuln) and then Heildleburg onto
Vampire B not of that clan.

Mata Hari simply performs these functions as one entity as opposed to a
combination of cards/vampires.

Even the "you may play" part of her text was originally solved by Clan
Impersonation.

There is nothing "wierd" about her.

Even Toreador Grand Ball where she taps as part of the play but after
that may untap normally since she is no longer Toreador can be
acheieved with other cards, its just easier with her.

David

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1116680203.5...@g47g2000cwa.googlegroups.com>,

X_Ze...@cox-internet.com writes:
>Could you use her to play Brujah Debate

Yes.

>and tap her as the largest
>Brujah?

No. That happens once it's in play, not when it's played.

By the time it's in play, her special ability has stopped working. So
she doesn't count as a Brujah for it.

>Could you use her to play Brujah Debate to hose other Brujah players
>and remain immune from its effect?

Yes. Just the same as if you played Clan Impersonation and then the CI
was burned immediately (by some effect).

Mata Hari effectively gives you a very temporary Clan Impersonation (or
"Sect Impersonation") which only exists for as long as you are playing
and resolving the card, and which is only acknowledged by the card she
plays/allows you to play. No other card notices the temporary "change",
and even the card you play stops noticing once you've played and
resolved it.

Same deal with Kemintiri advanced. The card she plays treats her as a
Justicar, Ventrue or Camarilla vampire, while she is playing and
resolving it. (Note that this doesn't actually give her extra votes, if
something had caused her to forfeit her own title - only the card she
plays knows she's got a pretend Justicar title.)

(She doesn't actually change, but this is a convenient lie for
understanding it.)

--
James Coupe

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <Pine.GSO.4.62.05...@eenie.cs.duke.edu>, Ankur

Gupta <agu...@cs.duke.edu> writes:
>So, the irony of my not finding something with google is particularly
>sweet, but either I'm stupid or it's not there:
>
>Does Mata Hari screw up pitching cards which have burn options and are
>tied to a clan?

No, you can still pitch them.

Some cards that have a requirement also have a burn option icon.
This icon means that a Methuselah who doesn’t control a minion
that meets the requirements may discard the card during any
Methuselah’s untap phase.

Mata Hari doesn't meet the requirements. She just lets you play *as if*
she met them.
